headline: Let rights decide the lane before product excitement decides.
copy: The rights desk turns each source into one clear use lane so the public pilot never confuses citation confidence with permission to reproduce or expand text.
boundary: This remains a static GitHub Pages prototype. It grants no production source authority, no reviewer account authority, no public launch permission, and no storage outside visible browser-local preview state.

lanes.title: Allowed
lanes.copy: Approved source and use scope are documented.

lanes.title: Review needed
lanes.copy: Edition, translator, or use rights are not yet clear.

lanes.title: Excerpt only
lanes.copy: Short cited reference is acceptable for demo, full text is not.

lanes.title: Blocked
lanes.copy: No learner-facing use until founder and reviewer clear it.

records.title: Steady action
records.confidence: High for citation, pending translation rights
records.allowedUse: Use as a cited source candidate for calm action examples.
records.boundary: Reflection support, not therapy, ritual instruction, or spiritual authority.

records.title: Cosmic-form quote context
records.confidence: High for citation, careful with popular wording
records.allowedUse: Use to correct the Oppenheimer quote category with restraint.
records.boundary: Do not call it a direct Vedic quote.

records.title: Gayatri mantra source candidate
records.confidence: Citation known, interpretation must be careful
records.allowedUse: Use source label and boundary before any explanation expands.
records.boundary: Study support only, not recitation authority.

records.title: Self-knowledge caution
records.allowedUse: Use only as a candidate until source edition is approved.
records.boundary: Do not turn into deterministic self-help advice.
records.next: Find an approved edition before public pilot.

checklist: Never treat citation confidence as reuse permission.
Show missing fields beside every learner-facing source card.
Move serious gaps into review tickets before public use.
Keep public pilot copy short, cited, and bounded.
